ask.prompt.task: Write one SPARQL 1.1 SELECT query that answers the question you were given (at the end of this text, or in the message that sent you here), over the RDF dataset described here. Answer with a single fenced ```sparql code block and nothing else. Project the people and organisations to show as variables, and include the dates and roles that matter.
ask.prompt.individuals: Work roles, document types and statuses (term "label" (class)):
ask.prompt.conventions:
Conventions of the data:
- People are foaf:Person and organisations foaf:Organization or a subclass; their names are foaf:name, foaf:firstName and :firstLastName, their IRIs rs:Name_Surname.
- Every relationship is a connection resource (a subclass of :Connection) linking its participants, never a direct property between two agents: employment and public office are :WorkConnection (bio:participant the person, :hasEconomicOrganizationParticipant the organisation, :hasWorkRole the role); ownership is vip:OwnershipConnection (vip:owner, vip:ownedCompany, vip:ownershipShare); schooling is :EducationalConnection (:hasStudent, :hasAcademicOrganization); kinship is vip:FamilyConnection and kumstvo vip:GodparentConnection (bio:participant both).
- Subclass and subproperty entailments are materialised: ?c a :Connection and ?c bio:participant ?p match every kind of connection and participant.
- Dates are :connectionStartDate and :connectionEndDate as xsd:gYear, xsd:gYearMonth or xsd:date; compare years with SUBSTR(STR(?date), 1, 4). A missing end date means unknown, never current.
- Every connection has :hasDocumentation; do not filter on sources unless asked.

report.title: Information wrong?
report.send.text: The simplest way. It opens a prepared report on GitHub, which needs a free account.
report.ai.text: Paste this prompt to an AI agent. It checks the sources and proposes a correction, asking your permission at every step.
about.tagline: Follow the money. To know where, follow the connections.
about.what: A map of documented connections between people of influence and organisations in Serbia, built from what reputable media and official registries report.
about.limit: A connection is a lead, not proof. Being related or having gone to the same school is not wrongdoing, and a missing connection does not mean none exists.
about.sources: Every entity and connection cites public documents with archived copies. Corrections are welcome through Report an error.
report.intro: Every claim here cites at least two public sources, listed with the record.
report.secondary: VIP is a secondary source: it collects what reputable media and official registries have published, and does not investigate or decide what is true. So the first step depends on where the error is.
report.case.source.text: Ask the outlet or registry that published it to correct or remove it. When the source no longer says it, VIP follows: a claim left without two sources is taken down.
report.case.ours.text: If our record says something its sources do not, or confuses two people, that is our mistake. Report it below and we will fix it.
